query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.hypothesis: A quinary refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) system with composition W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf (or similar low-VEC composition) processed via mechanical alloying for 40 hours followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at moderate temperatures (<1000°C) will simultaneously achieve a nanocrystalline grain size below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure (two distinct BCC solid solutions), thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or tailored multi-principal element powder mixture of refractory metals (e.g., W, Ta, Cr, V, Hf) with high atomic size mismatch and low valence electron concentration (VEC < 4.4) to favor BCC solid solutions.
generation.intervention: Mechanical alloying (ball milling) for 40 hours to induce severe plastic deformation and grain refinement, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at temperatures below 1000°C to consolidate the powder while retaining the nanocrystalline structure and preventing excessive grain growth or intermetallic precipitation.
generation.conditions: Processing under inert atmosphere (argon) to minimize oxygen contamination; SPS temperature controlled to stay below the threshold for intermetallic formation but sufficient for consolidation; milling time optimized to achieve full solid solution without excessive contamination.
generation.structural_mediator: Severe plastic deformation during mechanical alloying creates high dislocation density and grain refinement, while the low VEC and thermodynamic parameters (ΔH_mix, δ, Ω) stabilize a dual-phase BCC solid solution structure. The rapid consolidation via SPS locks in the nanocrystalline grain size.
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement via mechanical alloying (grain boundary strengthening) combined with solid solution strengthening from the dual-phase BCC structure. The low VEC prevents the formation of brittle intermetallics, while the nanocrystalline structure enhances yield strength via the Hall-Petch effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: A bulk RHEA with grain size <50 nm, dual-phase BCC solid solution structure, yield strength >2500 MPa, and improved ductility compared to cast forms, without brittle intermetallic phases.
generation.baseline: Cast refractory high-entropy alloys typically exhibit coarse grains (>100 nm), limited ductility, and often form brittle intermetallic phases due to slow cooling and segregation.
generation.boundary: The microstructure becomes unstable if SPS temperature exceeds 1000°C (leading to grain growth and potential intermetallic formation) or if milling time is excessive (>50 hours) causing oxygen/carbon contamination that promotes oxide precipitates (e.g., TiO) instead of solid solutions.
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition window for dual-phase BCC stability without intermetallics requires precise thermodynamic modeling; contamination during mechanical alloying may introduce oxide precipitates that alter the phase constitution. The long-term thermal stability of the nanocrystalline structure at elevated temperatures remains uncertain.
generation.falsification_experiment: Synthesize the proposed RHEA via mechanical alloying and SPS, then perform X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to confirm the presence of a dual-phase BCC solid solution and grain size <50 nm. Conduct compression testing to measure yield strength. If the microstructure shows significant grain growth (>50 nm), intermetallic formation, or yield strength <2000 MPa, the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, anneal the sample at 800°C for 100 hours to test thermal stability; if grain growth occurs rapidly, the nanocrystalline structure is unstable under the proposed conditions.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract In the quest of new materials that can withstand severe irradiation and mechanical extremes for advanced applications ( e.g . fission & fusion reactors, space applications, etc.), design, prediction and control of advanced materials beyond current material designs become paramount. Here, through a combined experimental and simulation methodology, we design a nanocrystalline refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) system. Compositions assessed under extreme environments and in situ electron-microscopy reveal both high thermal stability and radiation resistance. We observe grain refinement under heavy ion irradiation and resistance to dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation in the form of low defect generation and evolution, as well as no detectable grain growth. The experimental and modeling results—showing a good agreement—can be applied to design and rapidly assess other alloys subjected to extreme environmental conditions. Subject terms: Metals and alloys, Power stations

Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties

4.1. Influence of the Milling Time on the Properties of the Powders

The consequences of the variation in the milling time on the properties of the Al 0.3 NbTa 0.8 Ti 1.5 V 0.2 Zr RHEA powder (in stoichiometric ratio) have been assessed by changing the time of milling from 0 h up to 50 h while keeping the rotations per minute constant (250 RPM) under an argon atmosphere.

The XRD results show that after only 1 h of milling, the powders formed four phases: a main BCC1 phase and secondary BCC2, HCP1, and HCP2 phases. The powder microstructures are also significantly altered, as evidenced by SEM and EDS images, even though the segregation of all elements is very pronounced. After milling for 1 h, the Al element was fully dissolved into the other powders, due to higher ductility of its FCC crystal structure compared to the rest of the elements.

By increasing the milling time from 1 to 5 h, the total amount of the secondary phases decreases significantly, thus increasing the main BCC1 fraction.
